endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: For example: if the output is a score or percentage that can change over time, will previous scores or percentages be stored? Will patients have access to previously documented model outputs?

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether defining and documenting patient access to AI documentation and prior AI outputs improves transparency, trust, or care, and no supplied study documents the hazard itself. The recommendation currently rests on a single framework endorsement from the CHAI Responsible AI Guide.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The single endorsement is expert guidance, which reflects consensus judgment and does not substitute for comparative data on outcomes.

The CHAI Responsible AI Guide frames this as a should-level expectation and poses it as questions about whether changing scores are stored and whether patients can see them. That wording asks health systems to make and record a decision. It does not set a specific access standard, and no other supplied source adds a binding requirement.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that first measure how often patients are unable to see AI scores or documentation that influenced their care, and then compare health systems with and without documented access policies on patient comprehension, trust, correction of errors in the record, complaint rates, and staff burden of fulfilling requests.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence exists for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems cannot yet tell whether access policies would reach these patients in usable form, such as translated or plain-language explanations of AI outputs.
